blocks.text: Cottonwood 55+ homes for sale
Townhome complexes in Cottonwood MR

Name distinction, stated near the top so the two are never conflated: "Cottonwood MR" is a MAPLE RIDGE board sub-area (the MR suffix is the board's distinguisher). It is NOT Cottonwood Village in Chilliwack, which is a pad-rental manufactured-home park.
Streets, schools and getting around Cottonwood MR

items.t: The area's official anchors are Kanaka Creek Elementary at 11120 234A Street and Kanaka Creek, which runs through the area to the Fraser River; the residential area sits around Kanaka Creek Elementary (234A Street) and Alexander Robinson Elementary (238B Street), west of 240 Street and east of the Town Centre, with Kanaka Creek Regional Park along the creek.
Nearby areas: East Central and the Town Centre to the west, Albion to the east beyond 240 Street, Thornhill to the north.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the Cottonwood Drive cluster (The Meadows at Verigin's Ridge, Cottonwood Terrace, Carriage Lane), Kanaka Way (Cottonwood Grove), 236 Street (Maplewood Creek), 240 Street (Willow & Oak), 119 Avenue (Hollyhock) and 112 Avenue (The Falls).
Maple Ridge is a SnapStats-covered community.

Schools physically inside the area: Kanaka Creek Elementary (K–7), 11120 234A Street, and Alexander Robinson Elementary (K–7), 11849 238B Street, at the north edge; no secondary school is inside Cottonwood MR, and SD42 has no middle tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12). For the sample address 11120 234A Street the district locator gives Kanaka Creek Elementary and Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary.

Transit: the bus route named for the area is the 745 Haney Place / Cottonwood on TransLink's Haney Place route diagram; the 746 Haney Place / Albion interlines with the 745 at Jackson Road at 103 Avenue, forming one circular service; no West Coast Express station is in Cottonwood MR.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Cottonwood MR

items.t: Strata vs fee-simple — the core distinction, applied honestly here: three counted complexes are confirmed strata (The Meadows expressly, Cottonwood Terrace and Carriage Lane on their directories' strata-bylaw records); six are townhouse complexes whose tenure no public source checked states — for those, tenure is the first diligence step, because the two forms are bought completely differently. A strata townhouse buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees, and gets a Form B package. A fee-simple townhouse buyer owns the lot outright: NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees — municipal rules and any registered covenants/HOA only.

Form B diligence (strata complexes): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Depreciation reports and CRF (strata): since July 1, 2024, strata corporations with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, not deferrable by vote — the central check on the 1990s Cottonwood Drive stock (Cottonwood Terrace 1993, Hollyhock 1996, Carriage Lane 1998/1999). Since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund.

Co-op contrast (St. George's Village): a co-op purchase is a share purchase with board approval and the co-op's own transfer fee — no Form B, no strata fees in the Strata Property Act sense, and financing is lender-specific. Do not run a strata checklist on a co-op unit.

OCP citation — CONTESTED, flagged, never resolved by guessing: What is settled: no Cottonwood-specific area plan exists, so the OCP's general policies govern this sub-area. Two dated plan facts nearby: the Albion Area Plan was adopted October 28, 2025 (Albion is east of 240 Street, outside this sub-area), and the Lougheed Transit Corridor plan south of the area was ADOPTED January 27, 2026 per the City record (Council approved the OCP amendments January 27, 2026; OCP Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021 given third reading and adoption January 27, 2026; the corridor ends at 221 Street) — an earlier contrary reading of that corridor's status is noted in.

Suites and SSMUH: one secondary suite per lot, inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not in the Floodplain Area, building permit required; eligible single-detached and duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH rules, subject to zoning, bylaw and building code requirements — relevant to Cottonwood's detached streets, not to its townhouse complexes.

Creek and flood: Kanaka Creek is a salmon-bearing watercourse through the area and the regional park protects the creek corridor; whether a specific Cottonwood MR lot is in a mapped floodplain is per-lot on the City flood maps at MapleRidge.ca/Flood. No ALR land inside Cottonwood MR was identified on the sources read; ALR status is per-parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission's mapping, and an ALR residence cannot be stratified in any case (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)).

blocks.text: Good to know about Cottonwood MR

items.t: The City does not use this neighbourhood's name at all: Maple Ridge's neighbourhoods page does not list Cottonwood, and no Cottonwood area plan exists — the board name survives in listings and SnapStats while the City and the school district anchor the area by Kanaka Creek and its two elementary schools. With no area plan, rezoning expectations should be set by the OCP's general policies, not neighbourhood-plan promises.

Two housing things here are both called Cottonwood Park / Cottonwood-something and are not housing you can buy: Cottonwood Park (11600 Cottonwood Dr) is income-based subsidized rental run by Red Door Housing Society, and Cottonwood North Park (12111 238B St) is a City picnic park. Neither is a townhouse complex.

The co-op at the north edge is easy to mistake for a strata: St. George's Village's homes are townhouses and its listings read like strata listings, but its own membership form gives it away — a 55-year age qualification for MEMBERSHIP, clear title to the land held by the co-op, and a $3,500 share-transfer fee. It also sits beside St George Maple Ridge Anglican church (23500 Dewdney Trunk Rd), which is the likely source of a stray "St. Andrew's" seniors name that matches nothing in Maple Ridge.

The creek is working salmon habitat, not just scenery: Kanaka Creek Regional Park's Bell-Irving Hatchery supports chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout, the Canyon Trail runs 1.2 km one way from the hatchery to Cliff Falls, and the Riverfront Trails run 3 km one way at the creek oxbow and the Fraser River — the amenity the Cottonwood Drive complexes back onto, and the reason creek setbacks bind.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Cottonwood MR
Fee-simple lots

items.t: The stock: no Cottonwood area plan exists, so no City plan document sets out housing types for this area and city-wide housing rules apply; the residential streets around the two elementary schools are single-detached subdivisions under the RS zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019. The documented base is freehold houses, with secondary suites and SSMUH units as the added-density paths. Fee-simple is the default form: own title, no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.

Lot character, as the bylaw states it: the bylaw schedule gives a minimum lot area of 668 m² for RS-1; the other RS variants (RS-1a through RS-1d, RS-2, RS-3) carry their own schedules in the same bylaw, and the bylaw's residential zones also include RST, RT-1, RT-2 and RM-1 to RM-4.
Built strata ground is not land stock

blocks.text: Bare-land strata

items.t: Tenure trap on the area's edge — not land stock: St. George's Village Seniors Housing Co-operative (23580 Dewdney Trunk Road, north edge) holds its land as a co-operative — its membership form states the co-op "has clear title to land" and members buy shares, not lots.

blocks.text: Servicing, ALR, creek and assemblies

items.t: ALR vs non-ALR: no Agricultural Land Reserve land inside Cottonwood MR was identified on the official sources read; ALR status is per-parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission's mapping. No ALR split is stated.

Serviced vs unserviced: no well/septic position and no parcel-level servicing statement is documented for Cottonwood MR lots — held not confirmed parcel-by-parcel here; confirm municipal water/sewer connection with the City for the specific lot. No servicing claim is filled in.

Creek corridor is not buildable lot area: Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) follows Kanaka Creek through this part of Maple Ridge, with the Canyon Trail from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls (1.2 km one way) and Riverfront Trails (3 km one way) at the creek oxbow and the Fraser River; Metro Vancouver notes steep slippery cliffs along the creek, especially at Cliff Falls, and the Bell-Irving Hatchery supports chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout. Lots backing onto the creek carry setback/slope diligence — price buildable area, not creek-front gross area.

Land assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals: none documented for Cottonwood MR — no assembly, development site or rezoning proposal is named, and none is presented as for-sale inventory. South of the area, the Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan directs growth around future Bus Rapid Transit stations along Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road — a plan for corridor ground to the south, not a Cottonwood MR lot offering (adoption position).
: A presale project in Cottonwood MR is not verified (none verified).

Market context, labelled correctly: Maple Ridge IS a SnapStats-covered community, cited as community context only. SnapStats has NO land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined) — no detached figure is presented as a land figure. Per-sub-area median prices: Not verified (community level only).

items.t: Municipality: City of Maple Ridge. The City does not list Cottonwood as a named neighbourhood on its neighbourhoods page (which lists Albion/Kanaka, Port Hammond, Port Haney, Ruskin, Silver Valley, Thornhill, Town Centre, Webster's Corners, Whonnock and Yennadon), and no Cottonwood area plan appears on the City's area plans list.

Main roads: Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road are the east–west corridors south and north of the area, and Haney Place in the Town Centre is the bus exchange the area's routes connect to; local streets named in TransLink routing include 232 Street, 238B Street, Kanaka Way, 240 Street and 104 Avenue.

Transit: the bus route named for this area is the 745 Haney Place / Cottonwood; the 746 Haney Place / Albion interlines with the 745 at Jackson Road at 103 Avenue, forming one circular service; no West Coast Express station is in Cottonwood MR — the nearest stations are in the Town Centre.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Cottonwood MR

items.t: OCP — citation CONTESTED, flagged wherever met, resolved nowhere: What is settled: no Cottonwood-specific area plan was found; the area is covered by the OCP's general policies.

Neighbouring plans, precisely placed: the Albion Area Plan was adopted October 28, 2025 — Albion is east beyond 240 Street, outside this sub-area. Its effect is on corridor/Town Centre land, not on Cottonwood lots directly.

SSMUH / suites as the City states them — Maple Ridge's own figures, not Abbotsford's: one secondary suite per lot, inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not in the Floodplain Area, with a building permit required; eligible single-detached and duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH rules, subject to zoning, bylaw and building code requirements.

Flood / watercourse: Kanaka Creek is a salmon-bearing watercourse through the area and the regional park protects the creek corridor; the City's flood material covers the Fraser River floodplain, and whether a specific Cottonwood MR lot is in a mapped floodplain is not confirmed — check the City flood maps at MapleRidge.ca/Flood, and note suites are prohibited in the Floodplain Area (above).

ALR rules (where a parcel is confirmed ALR — none identified in Cottonwood MR): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); BC Assessment farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

items.t: No recreation centre, library or shopping centre sits inside the sub-area: the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre is at 11925 Haney Place in the Town Centre, Maple Ridge Public Library is at 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, and the nearest Town Centre centres named in the City's downtown guide are Haney Place Mall, 11900 Haney Place, and Valley Fair Mall, 22709 Lougheed Highway; grocery names/addresses beside the area were not confirmed on an official source. Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, provides 24/7 emergency services; the Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre is in Haney Place Mall, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

The bus is a loop, not a line: the 745 Cottonwood and 746 Albion interline at Jackson Road at 103 Avenue and run as one circular service to Haney Place Exchange, so trip time depends on which direction around the loop a lot's stop sits.

Two "Cottonwood Park" names, neither is buyable land: Cottonwood Park (11600 Cottonwood Drive) is subsidized non-profit rental run by Red Door Housing Society, and Cottonwood North Park (12111 238B Street) is a City picnic park — searches mix them up, and neither is a lot offering.

A 668 m² minimum is a house-lot figure, not an acreage figure — no parcel-size statistic beyond the zone schedules is published for the sub-area: Not verified, and no "typical acreage size" is invented here.

Boundaries: no City-published street-by-street boundary for Cottonwood MR was found; the residential area sits around Kanaka Creek Elementary (234A Street) and Alexander Robinson Elementary (238B Street), west of 240 Street and east of the Town Centre, with Kanaka Creek Regional Park along the creek. The area's official anchors are Kanaka Creek Elementary at 11120 234A Street and Kanaka Creek, which runs through the area to the Fraser River.

Main roads and commute: Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road are the east–west corridors south and north of the area, and Haney Place in the Town Centre is the bus exchange the area's routes connect to; local streets named in TransLink routing for the area include 232 Street, 238B Street, Kanaka Way, 240 Street and 104 Avenue. Parks and trails: Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) follows Kanaka Creek through this part of Maple Ridge, with trails for walking, cycling and horseback riding, the Canyon Trail from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls (1.2 km one way), Riverfront Trails (3 km one way) at the creek oxbow and the Fraser River, and the Bell-Irving Hatchery supporting chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout; Metro Vancouver notes steep slippery cliffs along the creek, especially at Cliff Falls.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Cottonwood MR

items.t: Zoning: City of Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019: — the bylaw contains the land-use and development regulations for every property in the city; its residential zones include RS-1, RS-1a, RS-1b, RS-1c, RS-1d, RS-2, RS-3, RST, RT-1, RT-2 and RM-1 to RM-4, and the bylaw schedule gives a minimum lot area of 668 m² for RS-1. Confirm the parcel's own zone schedule before relying on any lot figure.

Suites and added units: one secondary suite per lot, inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not in the Floodplain Area, with a building permit required; eligible single-detached and duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH rules, subject to zoning, bylaw and building code requirements. For a Cottonwood house lot, the suite / SSMUH position — not subdivision into acreage — is the added-value question, and the floodplain exclusion makes the City flood-map check part of the suite diligence.

Flood and watercourse diligence: the City's flood material covers the Fraser River floodplain, and whether a specific Cottonwood MR lot is in a mapped floodplain is not confirmed — check the City flood maps at MapleRidge.ca/Flood for the specific lot. Kanaka Creek setbacks apply next to the creek corridor, and the suite rule above excludes suites in the Floodplain Area — flood status is therefore a value item on creek-side and low lots, not a formality.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cottonwood MR

items.t: "Cottonwood" is a board name the City does not use: The City of Maple Ridge's neighbourhoods page lists ten named neighbourhoods and Cottonwood is not among them; the City and school district anchor this ground by Kanaka Creek and its two elementary schools instead.

The creek through the subdivision is a salmon system with a hatchery: Kanaka Creek Regional Park protects the creek corridor through this part of Maple Ridge, and the Bell-Irving Hatchery on it supports chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout; the Canyon Trail runs 1.2 km one way from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls and the Riverfront Trails run 3 km one way at the creek oxbow and the Fraser River. Creek-adjacent lots gain the trail system and inherit the setback / slope diligence in the same parcel.

The sample catchment address is the school's own address: The locator run used 11120 234A Street (Kanaka Creek Elementary's own address) and returned Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary (10445 245 Street), while SD42's east zone also runs Garibaldi Secondary (24789 Dewdney Trunk Road) and Thomas Haney Secondary. A Cottonwood listing that names a secondary school without a locator run for that address is ahead of the evidence.
